headline: Police fire teargas as garment workers clash with police in Mirpur
summary: Protests over minimum wage demands enter their fourth day, leading to violent clashes in Mirpur-11 and disrupting metro services.
details: RMG workers attempting to take to the streets in Dhaka clashed with police in Mirpur-11 today, prompting law enforcers to fire teargas shells and sound grenades to disperse the crowd.
Workers began walking out of several factories after 10:00 am and gathered in alleys on the western side of Mirpur-11, attempting to reach the main road.
Police chased the workers, who responded by hurling brickbats. The clashes continued for nearly half an hour before teargas and sound grenades forced the workers to retreat.
Following the dispersal of workers, leaders and activists of Jatiyatabadi Jubo Dal and Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal took positions on the main road, claiming they were there to prevent sabotage.
Nur Salam, convener of Pallabi Thana Jubo Dal, alleged that Awami League members had infiltrated the movement to create trouble, claiming they had caught several such individuals the previous day.
Touhidul Arif, deputy commissioner of the DMP's Public Order Management division, stated that 'miscreants with ulterior motives' were involved in the morning's unrest rather than actual workers.

The protests over demands for a higher minimum wage have now entered their fourth consecutive day, with tensions remaining high across various industrial areas including Ashulia, where 70 factories have shut down.

headline_marked: Garment workers [[block Dhaka-Tangail Highway]] in Gazipur unrest
headline: Garment workers block Dhaka-Tangail Highway in Gazipur unrest
summary: Police clear burning blockades of tyres and waste on the highway at two points in Gazipur following worker protests.
details: Garment workers attempted to block the Dhaka-Tangail Highway at two points in Gazipur on Tuesday morning, setting fire to tyres and waste to halt traffic.
The blockades occurred near Mouchak in Kaliakair around 8am and at the Naojor intersection around 9:30am, causing traffic jams between Joydebpur Chowrasta and Naojor.
Witnesses reported that workers blocked the highway in front of the Diganta Sweater factory at Naojor, where some protesters were also seen playing cricket on the road.
Gazipur Industrial Police Superintendent Md Amjad Hossain stated that law enforcers persuaded workers to leave the road at Mouchak and cleared the blockades at Naojor.
Police are now on high alert at various points along the highway to prevent further disorder and maintain traffic flow.
The unrest comes amid reports of clashes between workers and police, with some factories in Gazipur, Savar, and Ashulia shutting down due to the instability.
